audit.why: Kit: Hero's Entrance 180/160/140, range 4000/4750/5500. Galio's level 6 is a map spike, not a lane spike.

edits.before: Death Mark online — anyone below 60% in lane is now a math problem with a three-second answer.
edits.after: Death Mark online: Hero's Entrance is 180s at rank 1, so a solo kill has no rescue coming.

edits.before: First item spike: R-strings delete squishies through pots. Hunt the chip thresholds.
edits.after: First item: your roams beat his waveclear tempo — take the map while he holds mid.

edits.before: Late Zed picks: mark the carry, swap through the peel, and let the death note collect the paperwork.
edits.after: Late he is a taunt-and-shield teamfighter, not a duelist — keep marking his carries, never the wall.

edits.before: - Galio Justice Punch: matchup-defining — His dash knockup — he has no engage while it is down. Step up only on its downtime. - Budget W Living Shadow (swap) for emergencies and the R for opportunities — never swap them.
edits.after: - Justice Punch is 11s at rank 1 and 7s maxed — the knockup is his only engage, so step up the moment it is spent. - Shield of Durand taunts at 275 range on an 18s charge. - Keep the 20s Living Shadow as the swap out of it.

edits.before: W wide, E the slow, Q the scissor from two angles — half a bar of geometry he answered by standing still wrong.
edits.after: W wide, E for the slow, Q from two angles at 900 — never inside the 275 range where Shield of Durand taunts.

edits.before: R-ing into a banked stopwatch or held CC — the mark schedules YOUR death three seconds out when the answer was visible.
edits.after: R-ing a healthy Galio — his shield and resistances eat the string the mark repeats, and the taunt keeps you standing in it.

edits.before: W wide, E the slow, Q the scissor from two angles — half a bar of geometry he answered by standing still wrong.
edits.after: Above half he shrugs the repeat off behind Shield of Durand — the mark belongs on the carry you already chipped.

edits.before: R-ing into a banked stopwatch or held CC — the mark schedules YOUR death three seconds out when the answer was visible.
edits.after: Justice Punch knocks you up from 650 mid-string — with no shadow banked you eat the taunt and whatever follows it.

edits.before: That’s Galio’s bread-and-butter play — deny it and they run out of answers.
edits.after: His passive auto lands bonus area damage — the wind-up is the tell.

edits.before: The shadow swap is your only defense — both shadows spent entering is a cinematic with no second act.
edits.after: Hero's Entrance is 180s at rank 1 but shields his whole team — never open a fight into a fresh one.

edits.before: Galio wins by landing Justice Punch, denying your pattern, and starting the fight your kit wanted ten seconds later.
edits.after: Galio wins by knocking you up with Justice Punch into the taunt, then dropping Hero's Entrance on top of the fight.

edits.before: Carry through subpoenas — one marked carry per fight; your job is the threshold math and the swap you saved for their answer.
edits.after: Carry by marking whoever Galio is protecting — he cannot kill you himself, so the fight turns on whether you reach his carry.

edits.before: Ahead, audit the map: scissor Galio off every contact, mark the thresholds, and roam the crashes — fed Zed makes health bars legal documents.
edits.after: Ahead, take tempo: he waveclears and holds mid, so crash the wave, punish the whiffed Justice Punch, and roam before Hero's Entrance is back.

notes: Content whys[0] and whys[1] describe Shield of Durand only as a magic shield that blunts poke; Riot's text is a charged stance that ends in a taunt, which is the more dangerous half and is what actually decides level 1-3. I left those rows alone because their side ('Skill') is correct and the applier treats chart edits as an atomic group — a human may want to reword them. The kit tags Justice Punch with a 'terrain' flag; nothing in Riot's description creates terrain, so I treated it as a parsing misfire and wrote only the knockup.
